```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

`run_dietview()` opens an interactive [Shiny](https://shiny.posit.co/) app on a
prepared dataset. Use it to explore a diet on your own machine before you fix
the figures you will report. The chunks here are shown but not run, because the
app needs an interactive R session, the `shiny` package and, for the table,
`DT`.

```{r install}
install.packages(c("shiny", "DT"))
```

```{r launch}
library(DietView)

# the public ICES stomach data that ship with the package (see ?ices_diet)
# drop non-food items and nematodes (mostly parasites, not prey)
phylum <- ices_lineage$phylum[match(ices_diet$prey_aphia_id, ices_lineage$prey_aphia_id)]
dat <- ices_diet[ices_diet$item_type != "non_food" & !phylum %in% "Nematoda", ]

spec <- dv_spec(
  predator       = "predator_common",
  predator_latin = "predator_latin",
  stomach        = "stomach_id",
  prey_id        = "prey_aphia_id",
  prey_name      = "prey_name",
  weight         = "prey_weight_g",
  count          = "prey_count",
  digestion      = "digestion_label",
  covariates     = c("region", "year", "quarter")
)
prep <- dv_prepare(dat, spec, taxonomy = "table", lineage = ices_lineage,
                   verbose = FALSE)

run_dietview(prep)
```

The data are the ICES Stomach Content Database (ICES, Copenhagen), as
extracted in the R package stomachr (Lindmark 2026): 22 predators from the
North Sea, the Skagerrak-Kattegat and the Baltic Sea. The app opens on all
predators pooled; pick "Atlantic cod" and facet by `region` or `quarter` for a
first comparison. To compare periods or length classes, add those columns
before `dv_prepare()` and declare them, as in the article on covariates:

```{r launch-cov}
dat$period   <- dv_add_period(dat$year, breaks = c(2021.5, 2022, 2024),
                              labels = c("2022", "2023-2024"))
cod <- dat[dat$predator_common == "Atlantic cod", ]
cod$size_bin <- dv_size_bins(cod$length_cm, breaks = c(0, 20, 35, 50, 110))
spec_cod <- dv_spec(predator = "predator_common", stomach = "stomach_id",
                    prey_id = "prey_aphia_id", prey_name = "prey_name",
                    weight = "prey_weight_g", count = "prey_count",
                    digestion = "digestion_label",
                    covariates = c("region", "quarter", "period", "size_bin"))
run_dietview(dv_prepare(cod, spec_cod, taxonomy = "table",
                        lineage = ices_lineage, verbose = FALSE))
```

Records from 2020 and 2021 have no period; the app shows them in a separate
"NA" panel when you facet by `period`. That `NA` is a missing stratum, not an
unidentified prey.

`run_dietview(prep, currency = "numbers")` sizes the record view by the
number of individuals (`prey_count`) instead of the number of records. In the
ICES data almost all the unidentified material has no count, so it nearly
disappears from that view.

## What the app offers

- a predator selector, with "(all predators)" to pool every predator;
- a choice of what sizes the wedges: prey records (% of all records), weight
  (% of total weight) or the number of distinct prey items;
- a reporting-resolution selector: the full hierarchy, or rare prey merged up
  their lineage with `dv_aggregate_threshold()` in one of its three variants
  (pooled; pooled cross-predator, with a minimum number of predators; per
  predator), with the threshold as a number of stomachs;
- a covariate to facet by, which draws one sunburst per level, and a second
  covariate to cross with the first, which draws one sunburst per combination;
- a rank selector for the tables.

The tabs show the sunburst, the rank table (shares of records and weight at
the chosen rank, unidentified rows included), the frequency of occurrence at
that rank (`dv_fo_table()`) and, when the spec declares a digestion column,
the digestion diagnostic (`dv_digestion_diagnostic()`).

Pooled aggregations are computed on all predators before one is selected, so
a category means the same thing in every predator's view. Per-predator
aggregation counts stomachs within each predator, so its categories differ
between predators.

## Reproducing a view

The **Reproduce** tab shows the R script that rebuilds the current view, as
written by `dv_script()`, and offers the script, the prepared data it reads
(`dietview_prep.rds`) and the current tables (CSV) as downloads. The script
uses exported functions only, so it runs without the app, and its header
records the date, the DietView and R versions, the taxonomy source, the
reporting resolution and the column specification. The same script can be
written without the app:

```{r script}
s <- dv_script(prep, predator = "Atlantic cod", mode = "weight",
               aggregation = list(threshold = 8, scope = "pooled"))
s
```

## The app or the dashboard?

Use the app to explore on your own machine. Use `dv_build_html()` or
`dv_deploy()` to write a single HTML file that you can archive, email or put on
a web server, and that the reader opens without R.
